voices.note: the Master cited with ואמר מר inside Rava's analogy (32a.19); the text does not name him
Moses, whose words before God R' Elazar reports (32a.24)
anonymous redactorial voice: מאי אחילו, מאי אש של עצמות (32a.23), מאי בך (32a.24)

props.gloss_en: R' Elazar: 'and Moses besought (vayechal) the Lord' teaches that Moses stood in prayer before the Holy One until it made him ill
Rava: [he stood in prayer] until he annulled His vow for Him
and the Master said: [of 'he shall not annul (lo yachel) his word'] he himself does not annul, but others annul for him
Shmuel: it teaches that he gave himself over to death for them
as it says: 'and if not, blot me, I pray, out of Your book' (Ex 32:32)
Rav Yitzchak: it teaches that he caused the attribute of mercy to rest upon them
the Rabbis: it teaches that Moses said before the Holy One: Master of the world, it is a profanation for You to do such a thing
R' Eliezer HaGadol: it teaches that Moses stood in prayer before the Holy One until achilu seized him
R' Elazar: achilu is fire of the bones
Abaye: fire of the bones is ishta degarmei (Aramaic: fire of the bones)

Moses: had You sworn to them by heaven and earth, I would say that as heaven and earth pass away so does Your oath; now that You swore to them by Your great name, as Your great name lives and endures forever, so Your oath endures forever
